newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power up with outages, hurricane.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power up with outages, hurricane.

text.p: U.S. Midwest spot power prices rose late in the week as transmission line outages in Manitoba caused the province to import power from the U.S., and Hurricane Fran had traders expecting some East Coast generation facilities to cut power, industry sources said.
"The Manitoba thing sucked up a lot of power, the hurricane was coming, and on top of all that we had some sun and heat," said one Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) region trader.
Two Manitoba transmission lines with a total capacity of 3,000 megawatts (MW) were expected to be partially restored early next week after being shut down for storm damage.
